messages.subject: Summary of locus metrics
parts:
Hello group!

This is my genind object, from SilicoDart:

> gl

/// GENIND OBJECT /////////

 // 2,908 individuals; 134,480 loci; 134,480 alleles; size: 1.6 Gb

 // Basic content
   @tab:  2908 x 134480 matrix of allele counts
   @loc.n.all: number of alleles per locus (range: 1-1)
   @loc.fac: locus factor for the 134480 columns of @tab
   @all.names: list of allele names for each locus
   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)
   @type:  codom
   @call: .local(.Object = .Object, tab = ..1, ploidy = 2, ind.names = ..3, 
    loc.names = ..4, parallel = ..5)

 // Optional content
   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 1-448)
   @other: a list containing: loc.metrics 

//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

So, I'm trying to use dartR report functions, like as:

gl.report.callrate

gl.report.repavg

gl.report.secondaries

gl.report.maf

gl.report.hamming

gl.report.hwe

 

gl.report.monomorphs

gl.report.heterozygosity

But, only had success with the last two functions, for example:

> gl.report.monomorphs(gl)
Identifying monomorphic loci
  |=================================================================| 100%
Breakdown of 134480 loci
  Polymorphic loci: 134480 
  Monomorphic loci: 0 
  Loci with no scores (all NA): 0 


From the others, I couldn't, having these kind of reports:

> gl.report.callrate(gl)
Fatal Error: genlight object required for gl.report.callrate!
Error in gl.report.callrate(gl) : 
> gl.report.repavg(gl)
Fatal Error: Specify a genlight object
Error in gl.report.repavg(gl) : 

I would like to have a summary from all functions. But I can't understand why it works with a couple, and do not with the others functions.

I will really appreciate your support!
Thanks.

Peco

messages.author: be5831679f44e5dc
messages.subject: Re: Summary of locus metrics
parts:
Hi Peco,

As you can see in the error, those functions require a genlight object. As you note, your data is a genind object. You can change this using:

gl <- gi2gl(gl)

Cheers,

Renee

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Summary of locus metrics
parts:
Hi Peco,

 

Though the conversion gi2gl may work in terms of format, be careful with this.

 

The reason why silico darts are stored as genind (not genlight) is that it is a haplotype kind of format (ploidy =1) and a conversion into genlight may not be “good”.

 

Without checking I can see that filters like RepAvg would work, but clearly MAF would not.

 

I think also PCoA should work. Better to look into the adegenet vignettes for genind object and see what you can do.

 

A simple

 

summary(gi)

 

gives you some summary statistics (might be slow depending on the number of loci).

 

In principle you can also use the package PopGenReport (but it was meant for maybe max 50 loci and hence it may break especially the pdf version of the package).

 

Admittedly the support for silicos is lacking currently but that will change in the future (just did not come around to work on it).

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: Summary of locus metrics
parts:
Hi Peco,

dartR does not yet support SilicoDArT analyses. SilicoDArT data comprise presence/absence data for sequence tags (1's and 0's). Essentially they are the same as the null alleles (missing data) in your SNP dataset, except that the SNP dataset is optimized for calling SNPs and the SilicoDArT dataset is optimized for calling presence or absence of the sequence tags.

So, as Bernd has indicated, simply converting your genind object (containing the SilicoDArT data) to a genlight object is unlikely to be terribly reliable for all but a few analyses.

What we need is for someone with a deep interest in SilicoDArT to write scripts for incorporation into dartR. It probably won't happen at our end until we have a project that demands them. A little challenge for you perhaps :)

All the best,

A
